archetype.name: Retooling (defense-first)
archetype.definition: After three straight seasons at the bottom, Washington has put veterans like Anthony Davis and Trae Young around a young core, and for now it plays like a lottery-to-fringe team rather than a cellar dweller.

report.headline: Defense finally exists; a broken jump shot is why it still isn't winning
report.take:
For the first time in years the Wizards are not the worst team on the floor most nights. They come off records of 15-67, 18-64 and 17-65, ranked 30th on the site each time, and they sit 4-6 and 22nd. The record is an honest one. W vs Pt Diff is exactly 0, and the margin implies the same 4 wins they have. This is a below-average team that has stopped being a historically bad one, and almost all of that change is on defense.

The defensive rating is 113.9, 16th in the league. Last season it was 122.7, the worst in the league. Opponents are shooting 62.4% at the rim, down from 67.5% a year ago. With Davis, Alex Sarr and Deandre Ayton taking most of the frontcourt minutes, that looks structural. The frontcourt grades B+, the best group on the roster. The offense has not followed. The offensive rating is 109.1 (23rd), the 3P % is 30.2 (28th), and the team takes threes at the 28th-highest rate. Davis is the engine: tabRank 7 among power forwards, a 29.6 USG %, and the team is +13.3 with him on the floor. Kyshawn George, 11th on the shooting-guard tab, has a 60.5 TS % and an On-Off of +12.3, and he has been the most efficient high-usage player here. Young's On-Off is -5.5 and Bilal Coulibaly's is -14, which says the lineups around those two have not worked.

The numbers hide two things running in opposite directions. The defense is getting help it probably won't keep. Opponents are hitting 31.7% from three, 4th-lowest, against a league average of 34.8. Every recent Washington team allowed over 36%. Expect some of that to come back. The shooting slump should ease somewhat, since last year's team made 35.9%, but the low volume means even a recovery adds less than it would elsewhere. The rebounding is a genuine flaw. ORB % is 22.2 (29th) and DRB % is 69 (26th), and opposing centers are piling up 16.3 boards a game.

The direction is the worry. October was 3-3 with the team roughly breaking even (110.5 scored, 109.67 allowed a game). November is 1-3, allowing 116.75 a game and scoring 103.75, and it bottomed out with a 75-114 loss at OKC. The 33-win pace is a real step forward on paper. Hitting it will depend on Davis staying on the floor, since he is listed Day-To-Day, and on the threes starting to fall before the opponent luck runs out.

strengths.title: A defense rebuilt from the bottom
strengths.body: The defense has gone from the league's worst to the middle of the pack. The DRtg is 113.9 (16th), against 122.7 and a 30th-place Def Rank last season. The rim protection is the durable part: Opp Rim FG % is 62.4, 9th in the league, while the last three teams all allowed over 67%. Some of the gain rests on opponents' cold three-point shooting, so expect a modest slide rather than a collapse.

strengths.title: Davis and George drive the good minutes
strengths.body: Davis (tabRank 7 at his position, On-Off +13.3) and George (TS % 60.5, On-Off +12.3) are the two players the team clearly wins with. Together they explain why the frontcourt grades B+ even as the wings sit at D+. George's efficiency at a 23.9 USG % looks like the most important development on the roster. Davis's on-court value is not in question; his availability is.

strengths.title: They take care of the ball
strengths.body: A TOV % of 13.1 ranks 9th, better than the league's 13.8. With a shooting profile this poor, not giving away extra possessions is what keeps the offense at 23rd instead of the bottom. It is a habit-driven number that usually holds.

concerns.title: Few threes, and they aren't falling
concerns.body: The Wizards shoot 30.2% from three (28th) and take them at a 37 3PA Rate (also 28th), well below the league's 43. Tre Johnson has a 46.7 TS % and a -9 BPM on 22.3 USG %, which concentrates possessions in poor hands. Last year's team made 35.9%, so some bounce-back is likely. The shot diet still caps the offense's ceiling.

concerns.title: Losing the glass on both ends
concerns.body: An ORB % of 22.2 ranks 29th and a DRB % of 69 ranks 26th, so the team neither extends its own possessions nor ends opponents'. Opposing centers grab 16.3 rebounds a game against them, 28th, and well over their own averages. This has been a weakness in recent seasons too, and it is the leak most likely to undo the defensive gains against big teams.

concerns.title: Opponent shooting luck will fade
concerns.body: Opponents are making 31.7% of their threes (4th-lowest), 3.1 points under the league average. Every Washington team in the sheet's history allowed at least 36.1%. Three-point defense is the noisiest part of a defensive rating, so the 16th-ranked DRtg probably overstates where this group really is.

trend.note: October was a break-even 3-3, but November is 1-3 with the offense down to 103.75 a game. Over the last five the differential is -7.2 a game, worse than the season as a whole.

weekAhead.headline: Four top-ten opponents and two back-to-backs test a sputtering offense
weekAhead.body:
Five games, and four are against teams in the site's top ten: Detroit twice (6-3, 9th), Houston (7-3, 6th) and Memphis (6-3, 8th). The week also has two back-to-backs, at Indiana then home to Detroit, and Houston then Memphis. That is a hard draw for a team whose Davis is Day-To-Day. Detroit's defense is the second-best by DRtg at 105.9, and it forces turnovers at the 4th-highest rate. That is exactly the wrong matchup for an offense that already struggles to score and survives on ball security.

The one even game is at Indiana (3-7, 23rd), a team with an F frontcourt and the league's worst ORB %. That is the night Washington's size should finally win the glass. Escaping with two wins would be a good week. One is the more likely outcome, especially if Davis misses time.

keyMatchups.title: Detroit's defense against Washington's shooting
keyMatchups.body: Detroit allows a 49.5 Opp eFG %, 2nd in the league, and holds point guards to the fewest points-rebounds-assists of any team. That squeezes Young. The opening is inside: opposing centers grab the most rebounds against Detroit (rank 30), so Sarr and Ayton have a real chance on the offensive glass in both meetings.

keyMatchups.title: Houston's size hits Washington's weak spot
keyMatchups.body: Houston has an A+ frontcourt and the 6th-best ORB %, against a Wizards DRB % ranked 26th. Houston also holds power forwards to 14.4 points, 4th-fewest and well under their norms, which makes it the hardest Davis matchup of the week. Second-chance points could decide this one.

keyMatchups.title: Indiana is the winnable game
keyMatchups.body: Indiana has an F frontcourt and the worst ORB % in the league (21, 30th), so this is the one opponent Washington can outrebound. Indiana also lets centers score 21.9 points a game (26th), a clear opening for Sarr and Ayton.

weekAhead.watch: Whether Anthony Davis, listed Day-To-Day, plays through two back-to-backs; the team's best minutes run through him.

restOfSeason.body:
The 33-win pace is a fair ceiling, not a floor. The rim defense and ball security look real, and the shooting should improve from 30.2% toward something closer to last year. Opponent three-point luck will cut the other way, though, and the rebounding problem doesn't fix itself. Netting those out leaves a team that is meaningfully better than the last three but still below average, and the season hinges on Davis's health and George's growth. A final record in the high 20s to mid 30s, with a Net Rtg somewhere around -6.5 to -3, is the likely band.

What regresses: opponents' 3P % should drift up toward 33.5–35.5, costing the defense its middle-of-the-pack rank. What improves: Washington's own 3P % should climb into the 32–34.5 range, which would lift the offense out of the bottom eight. Watch Dybantsa (six games so far, 23.6 USG %) as a second-half variable. His efficiency rising would give the wings their first real contributor.
swingFactors: Three-point shooting recovering toward last year's level
Holding the rim defense as opponent 3P luck fades

confidence.note: Ten games; opponent 3P % noise; Davis's Day-To-Day status.
